decisions.choice: parable: a story that compares and teaches
decisions.reason: As in chapter 13, a parable sets a picture beside the truth it teaches.

decisions.choice: story
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain word for a teaching story.

decisions.choice: parábola (L, B); historia (R)
decisions.reason: The term used throughout Matthew, recorded once in this passage. Readable says "historia", as the English Readable says "story" (meaning decision m1). Jesus still speaks to the leaders, so the plural "you" is the ustedes / vosotros setting.

decisions.choice: parabole (L, B); histoire (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 4 and 12: Readable names what follows as a story, as the English Readable does; 21:45 says "les histoires" in the same way.

decisions.choice: mfano (L, B); hadithi (R)
decisions.reason: The term used throughout Matthew, recorded once in this passage. Readable says "hadithi" (story), as the English Readable says "story" (meaning decision m1).

source.text: Ἄνθρωπος ἦν οἰκοδεσπότης ὅστις ἐφύτευσεν ἀμπελῶνα καὶ φραγμὸν αὐτῷ περιέθηκεν καὶ ὤρυξεν ἐν αὐτῷ ληνὸν καὶ ᾠκοδόμησεν πύργον, καὶ ἐξέδετο αὐτὸν γεωργοῖς, καὶ ἀπεδήμησεν.

records.literal_gloss: A man there was a master of a house who planted a vineyard and a fence it placed around and dug in it a winepress and built a tower, and rented out it to farmers, and traveled abroad.

en.L: There was a man, a master of a house, who planted a vineyard and put a fence around it and dug a winepress in it and built a tower, and leased it to farmers and went abroad.
en.B: A man who owned an estate planted a vineyard. He set a hedge around it, cut a pit for a winepress, and put up a watchtower. Then he leased it to tenant farmers and went abroad.
en.R: A man owned some land, and he planted grapevines on it. He put a fence around the vineyard. He dug out a place to crush the grapes. He built a tall tower so a guard could watch over it. Then he let some farmers use the vineyard and pay him rent. After that he went away to another country.

es.L: Había un hombre, señor de una casa, que plantó una viña, y le puso una cerca alrededor, y cavó en ella un lagar, y construyó una torre, y la dio en arriendo a agricultores, y se fue al extranjero.
es.B: Un hombre que tenía una hacienda plantó una viña. La rodeó con un cerco, excavó un lagar y levantó una torre de vigilancia. Luego se la arrendó a unos agricultores y se fue al extranjero.
es.R: Un hombre tenía un terreno, y allí plantó una viña. Le puso una cerca alrededor. Cavó un lugar para aplastar las uvas. Construyó una torre alta para que un guardia pudiera vigilar la viña. Después dejó que unos agricultores usaran la viña a cambio de pagarle una renta. Luego se fue a otro país.

fr.L: Il y avait un homme, un maître de maison, qui a planté une vigne, l’a entourée d’une clôture, y a creusé un pressoir et a bâti une tour ; puis il l’a louée à des vignerons et est parti à l’étranger.
fr.B: Un propriétaire a planté une vigne. Il l’a entourée d’une haie, y a creusé une cuve pour le pressoir et a bâti une tour de garde. Puis il l’a louée à des vignerons et s’en est allé dans un autre pays.
fr.R: Un homme avait un terrain, et il y a planté de la vigne. Il a mis une clôture tout autour. Il a creusé un trou dans la roche pour écraser le raisin. Il a construit une haute tour d’où un gardien pouvait surveiller la vigne. Ensuite, il a laissé des cultivateurs s’occuper de la vigne, et ils devaient lui payer un loyer. Puis il est parti dans un autre pays.

sw.L: Palikuwa na mtu, bwana wa nyumba, ambaye alipanda shamba la mizabibu, akaweka ua kulizunguka, akachimba ndani yake kisima cha kukamulia zabibu, akajenga mnara, akalikodisha kwa wakulima, akaenda ng'ambo.
sw.B: Mtu mmoja aliyekuwa na ardhi alipanda shamba la mizabibu. Akaweka ua kulizunguka, akachonga shimo la kukamulia zabibu, akajenga mnara wa ulinzi. Kisha akawakodishia wakulima shamba hilo, akaenda ng'ambo.
sw.R: Mtu mmoja alikuwa na ardhi, akapanda mizabibu ndani yake. Aliweka ua kulizunguka shamba hilo. Alichimba mahali pa kukamulia zabibu. Alijenga mnara mrefu ili mlinzi aweze kulilinda shamba. Kisha aliwaruhusu wakulima fulani walitumie shamba hilo na kumlipa kodi. Baada ya hapo alisafiri kwenda nchi nyingine.

decisions.choice: planting, fence, winepress, tower: Isaiah 5:1-2
decisions.reason: Isaiah sings of a vineyard its owner prepared in just this way. There the vineyard is the house of Israel and the owner is the LORD (Isaiah 5:7). Jesus' hearers would know the song.

decisions.choice: leased it to farmers: tenants who worked the land and paid the owner part of the crop
alternatives: hired laborers paid by the day
decisions.reason: Landowners who lived far away often let land to tenant farmers, who paid rent in produce.

decisions.choice: winepress: a pit cut in the rock to tread grapes
decisions.reason: Grapes were trodden in a shallow basin, and the juice ran into a lower pit, as the verb "dug" shows.

decisions.choice: no spans for the owner or his son
alternatives: spans because they stand for God and Jesus
decisions.reason: The owner and his son are figures in a parable, so their pronouns take no deity_pronoun span, like the sower and the master in other parables.

decisions.choice: tenant farmers (B); farmers who use the vineyard and pay him rent (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that the farmers were tenants.

decisions.choice: agricultores (L, R); arrendatarios (B, from verse 34)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is simply "farmers"; the story makes them tenants (meaning decision m2). Balanced says "arrendatarios" once the lease has been told, as the English Balanced says "tenants"; "labradores" sounds old to many readers.

decisions.choice: the parable in the passé composé at every level; narration around it in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R), with Matthew's historic presents kept at Literal ("ils lui disent", "Jésus leur dit")
alternatives: passé simple for the parable at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: Jesus tells the story, so it keeps the tenses of speech, as the style guide sets and as Mark 12:1-9 does. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: des vignerons (L, B); des cultivateurs (R)
decisions.reason: As Mark 12: "vignerons" are the men who work a vineyard, and "louer à" already shows they were tenants (m2); Readable uses the plainer "cultivateurs" and says how the lease worked.

decisions.choice: kisima cha kukamulia zabibu (L); shimo la kukamulia zabibu (B); mahali pa kukamulia zabibu (R)
decisions.reason: The winepress was a pit cut in the rock where grapes were trodden (meaning decision m3). "Shinikizo" is a press and is not known to most readers; the phrase says what the place was for.

source.text: ὅτε δὲ ἤγγισεν ὁ καιρὸς τῶν καρπῶν, ἀπέστειλεν τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ πρὸς τοὺς γεωργοὺς λαβεῖν τοὺς καρποὺς αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: When then drew near the season of the fruits, he sent the slaves of him to the farmers to receive the fruits of him.

en.L: And when the season of the fruits drew near, he sent his slaves to the farmers to receive his fruits.
en.B: When harvest time came near, he sent his servants to the tenants to collect his share of the crop.
en.R: When it was time to pick the grapes, the owner sent his servants to the farmers to get his share of the grapes.

es.L: Y cuando se acercó el tiempo de los frutos, envió a sus esclavos a los agricultores para recibir sus frutos.
es.B: Cuando se acercaba la cosecha, envió a sus siervos a los arrendatarios para cobrar la parte de la cosecha que le correspondía.
es.R: Cuando llegó el tiempo de recoger las uvas, el dueño envió a sus siervos a los agricultores para recibir su parte de las uvas.

fr.L: Et quand le temps des fruits s’est approché, il a envoyé ses esclaves aux vignerons pour recevoir ses fruits.
fr.B: Quand le temps de la récolte est arrivé, il a envoyé ses serviteurs chez les vignerons pour recevoir sa part de la récolte.
fr.R: Quand le moment de cueillir le raisin est arrivé, le propriétaire a envoyé ses serviteurs chez les cultivateurs pour recevoir sa part du raisin.

sw.L: Basi msimu wa matunda ulipokaribia, aliwatuma watumwa wake kwa wakulima wachukue matunda yake.
sw.B: Wakati wa mavuno ulipokaribia, aliwatuma watumishi wake kwa wakulima ili wachukue sehemu yake ya mavuno.
sw.R: Wakati wa kuchuma zabibu ulipofika, mwenye shamba aliwatuma watumishi wake kwa wakulima ili wampatie sehemu yake ya zabibu.

decisions.choice: slaves: the owner's slaves, sent with his authority
decisions.reason: The word means a slave, a person owned by a master. The prophets are called God's slaves (Jeremiah 7:25; Amos 3:7), and the story points to them.

decisions.choice: his fruits: the share of the crop that belonged to the owner
decisions.reason: The pronoun most naturally refers to the owner. Under a lease he was owed part of the harvest.

decisions.choice: his share of the crop (B); his share of the grapes (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the owner was owed.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that they were owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: esclavos (L); siervos (B, R)
decisions.reason: The terms used throughout Matthew, recorded once in this passage: the owner's slaves act for him (meaning decision m1), as servants sent with his authority.

decisions.choice: esclaves (L); serviteurs (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms, as the English and Mark 12: Literal keeps that the men were owned (m1), Balanced and Readable say "serviteurs", the role they play as the owner's envoys. This holds for the whole parable.

decisions.choice: watumwa (L); watumishi (B, R)
decisions.reason: The terms used throughout Matthew, recorded once in this passage: the owner's slaves act for him (meaning decision m1), as servants sent with his authority.

source.text: καὶ λαβόντες οἱ γεωργοὶ τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ ὃν μὲν ἔδειραν, ὃν δὲ ἀπέκτειναν, ὃν δὲ ἐλιθοβόλησαν.

records.literal_gloss: And having taken the farmers the slaves of him, one they beat, another they killed, another they stoned.

en.L: And the farmers, taking his slaves, beat one, killed another, and stoned another.
en.B: The tenants grabbed his servants. One they beat up, another they killed, and another they pelted with stones.
en.R: But the farmers grabbed the owner's servants. They beat one of them. They killed another one. And they threw stones at another one.

es.L: Y los agricultores, agarrando a sus esclavos, a uno lo apalearon, a otro lo mataron y a otro lo apedrearon.
es.B: Los arrendatarios agarraron a sus siervos. A uno le dieron una paliza, a otro lo mataron y a otro lo atacaron a pedradas.
es.R: Pero los agricultores agarraron a los siervos del dueño. A uno lo golpearon. A otro lo mataron. Y a otro le tiraron piedras.

fr.L: Et les vignerons, ayant saisi ses esclaves, ont battu l’un, ont tué l’autre, et ont lapidé l’autre.
fr.B: Les vignerons se sont saisis de ses serviteurs : ils ont roué de coups l’un, tué un autre et lapidé un troisième.
fr.R: Mais les cultivateurs ont attrapé les serviteurs du propriétaire. Ils ont frappé l’un d’eux. Ils ont tué un autre. Et ils ont jeté des pierres sur un autre.

sw.L: Na wakulima, wakiwa wamewashika watumwa wake, huyu walimchapa, yule walimuua, na mwingine walimpiga mawe.
sw.B: Wakulima waliwakamata watumishi wake. Mmoja wakamchapa vibaya, mwingine wakamuua, na mwingine wakamtupia mawe.
sw.R: Lakini wakulima waliwakamata watumishi wa mwenye shamba. Mmoja walimpiga. Mwingine walimuua. Na mwingine walimtupia mawe.

decisions.choice: beaten, killed, stoned: the way the prophets were treated
alternatives: violence with no meaning beyond the story
decisions.reason: Zechariah son of Jehoiada was stoned in the temple court (2 Chronicles 24:21), and Jesus will speak of Jerusalem stoning those sent to her (23:37).

decisions.choice: stoned: pelted with stones, often to death
decisions.reason: Stoning was a way of putting someone to death, but the verb itself means to throw stones at someone.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it, and Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: πάλιν ἀπέστειλεν ἄλλους δούλους πλείονας τῶν πρώτων, καὶ ἐποίησαν αὐτοῖς ὡσαύτως.

records.literal_gloss: Again he sent other slaves more than the first, and they did to them likewise.

en.L: Again he sent other slaves, more than the first, and they did the same to them.
en.B: So the owner sent other servants, a larger group than the first, and the tenants treated them the same way.
en.R: So the owner sent more servants, more than the first time. But the farmers did the same things to them.

es.L: De nuevo envió otros esclavos, más que los primeros, y les hicieron lo mismo.
es.B: Entonces el dueño envió otros siervos, un grupo más numeroso que el primero, y los arrendatarios los trataron de la misma manera.
es.R: Así que el dueño envió más siervos, más que la primera vez. Pero los agricultores les hicieron lo mismo.

fr.L: De nouveau il a envoyé d’autres esclaves, plus nombreux que les premiers, et ils les ont traités de même.
fr.B: Le propriétaire a alors envoyé d’autres serviteurs, plus nombreux que les premiers, et les vignerons les ont traités de la même façon.
fr.R: Alors le propriétaire a envoyé d’autres serviteurs, plus nombreux que la première fois. Mais les cultivateurs leur ont fait la même chose.

sw.L: Tena alituma watumwa wengine, idadi kubwa kuliko wale wa kwanza, na wakawafanyia hivyo hivyo.
sw.B: Basi mwenye shamba alituma watumishi wengine, kundi kubwa kuliko lile la kwanza, na wakulima wakawafanyia vivyo hivyo.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo mwenye shamba alituma watumishi wengi zaidi kuliko mara ya kwanza. Lakini wakulima waliwafanyia mambo yale yale.

decisions.choice: more than the first: more in number
decisions.reason: The word can mean greater in number or in rank. Here more slaves are sent.

decisions.choice: the owner; the tenants (B), the farmers (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who sent and who acted.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it, and Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: ὕστερον δὲ ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ λέγων· Ἐντραπήσονται τὸν υἱόν μου.

records.literal_gloss: Last then he sent to them the son of him saying, They will respect the son of me.

en.L: And later he sent his son to them, saying, 'They will respect my son.'
en.B: Finally he sent his son to them. He told himself, 'They will show respect to my son.'
en.R: Finally the owner sent his son to them. He thought, 'The farmers will respect my son.'

es.L: Y por último les envió a su hijo, diciendo: “Respetarán a mi hijo”.
es.B: Por último les envió a su hijo. Se dijo: “A mi hijo lo respetarán”.
es.R: Al final, el dueño les envió a su hijo. Pensó: “A mi hijo, los agricultores lo van a respetar”.

fr.L: Et en dernier, il leur a envoyé son fils, disant : “Ils respecteront mon fils.”
fr.B: Finalement, il leur a envoyé son fils, en se disant : “Ils auront du respect pour mon fils.”
fr.R: À la fin, le propriétaire a envoyé son fils chez eux. Il pensait : “Les cultivateurs vont respecter mon fils.”

sw.L: Hatimaye alimtuma kwao mwana wake, akisema, 'Watamheshimu mwanangu.'
sw.B: Mwishowe alimtuma mwanawe kwao. Akajiambia, 'Mwanangu watamheshimu.'
sw.R: Hatimaye mwenye shamba alimtuma mwanawe. Alifikiri, 'Wakulima watamheshimu mwanangu.'

decisions.choice: his son: in the story, the owner's son; in its meaning, Jesus
decisions.reason: The son comes after all the slaves and is the heir (21:38). God has called Jesus his beloved Son (3:17), and the leaders see that the story is about them (21:45).

decisions.choice: later: at last, after all the others
decisions.reason: The word means afterward or finally; the son is the last one sent.

decisions.choice: respect: feel shame before, and so treat with honor
decisions.reason: The verb means to turn back in shame before someone, and so to show them respect.

decisions.choice: He told himself (B); He thought (R)
decisions.reason: The owner speaks his hope rather than giving an order, so Balanced and Readable make it his thought.

source.text: οἱ δὲ γεωργοὶ ἰδόντες τὸν υἱὸν εἶπον ἐν ἑαυτοῖς· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ κληρονόμος· δεῦτε ἀποκτείνωμεν αὐτὸν καὶ σχῶμεν τὴν κληρονομίαν αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: The but farmers having seen the son said among themselves, This is the heir; come let us kill him and let us have the inheritance of him;

en.L: But the farmers, seeing the son, said among themselves, 'This is the heir; come, let us kill him and have his inheritance.'
en.B: The tenants, though, saw the son and said to one another, 'Here is the one who will inherit the vineyard. Come on, if we kill him, his inheritance will be ours.'
en.R: But when the farmers saw the son, they talked among themselves. They said, 'This son will own the vineyard someday. Let us kill him! Then the vineyard will belong to us.'

es.L: Pero los agricultores, al ver al hijo, dijeron entre sí: “Este es el heredero; {{plural_you:vengan|venid}}, matémoslo y quedémonos con su herencia”.
es.B: Pero cuando los arrendatarios vieron al hijo, se dijeron unos a otros: “Este es el que va a heredar la viña. {{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}}, si lo matamos, su herencia será nuestra”.
es.R: Pero cuando los agricultores vieron al hijo, hablaron entre ellos. Dijeron: “Este hijo va a ser el dueño de la viña algún día. ¡Vamos a matarlo! Así la viña será nuestra”.

fr.L: Mais les vignerons, voyant le fils, se sont dit entre eux : “Celui-ci est l’héritier ; venez, tuons-le et ayons son héritage.”
fr.B: Mais en voyant le fils, les vignerons se sont dit les uns aux autres : “C’est lui qui doit hériter de la vigne. Allons, tuons-le, et son héritage sera à nous !”
fr.R: Mais quand les cultivateurs ont vu le fils, ils se sont parlé entre eux. Ils ont dit : “C’est le fils qui recevra la vigne un jour. Tuons-le ! Comme ça, la vigne sera à nous !”

sw.L: Lakini wakulima, wakimwona mwana, wakasema miongoni mwao, 'Huyu ni mrithi; njooni, tumuue, tuwe na urithi wake.'
sw.B: Lakini wakulima walipomwona mwana huyo, waliambiana, 'Huyu ndiye atakayerithi shamba hili. Njooni, tukimuua, urithi wake utakuwa wetu.'
sw.R: Lakini wakulima walipomwona mwana huyo, walizungumza wao kwa wao. Walisema, 'Siku moja mwana huyu atakuwa mwenye shamba hili. Tumuue! Kisha shamba litakuwa letu.'

decisions.choice: kill the heir and take the inheritance: a scheme to keep the land
decisions.reason: With the heir dead and the owner far away, the tenants hope the land will be left to those who hold it.

decisions.choice: come, let us kill him: the words of Joseph's brothers
decisions.reason: Joseph's brothers said almost the same when they saw him coming (Genesis 37:20 in the Greek Old Testament).

decisions.choice: the vineyard
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the son would inherit.

source.text: καὶ λαβόντες αὐτὸν ἐξέβαλον ἔξω τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος καὶ ἀπέκτειναν.

records.literal_gloss: And having taken him they cast out outside of the vineyard and killed.

en.L: And taking him, they threw [him] out of the vineyard and killed [him].
en.B: They took hold of him, forced him outside the vineyard, and killed him.
en.R: So they grabbed the son and threw him out of the vineyard. Then they killed him.

es.L: Y agarrándolo, [lo] arrojaron fuera de la viña y [lo] mataron.
es.B: Lo agarraron, lo sacaron a la fuerza de la viña y lo mataron.
es.R: Entonces agarraron al hijo y lo echaron de la viña. Después lo mataron.

fr.L: Et l’ayant saisi, ils [l’]ont jeté hors de la vigne et [l’]ont tué.
fr.B: Ils se sont saisis de lui, l’ont poussé hors de la vigne et l’ont tué.
fr.R: Alors ils ont attrapé le fils et l’ont jeté hors de la vigne. Puis ils l’ont tué.

sw.L: Na baada ya kumshika, walimtupa nje ya shamba la mizabibu, na kumuua.
sw.B: Wakamshika, wakamsukuma nje ya shamba la mizabibu, kisha wakamuua.
sw.R: Basi wakamkamata mwana huyo na kumtoa nje ya shamba. Kisha wakamuua.

decisions.choice: thrown out and then killed: the son dies outside the vineyard
decisions.reason: Mark 12:8 has the son killed and then thrown out. Matthew's order may look ahead to Jesus' death outside the city (27:31-33; Hebrews 13:12).

source.text: ὅταν οὖν ἔλθῃ ὁ κύριος τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος, τί ποιήσει τοῖς γεωργοῖς ἐκείνοις;

records.literal_gloss: When therefore comes the lord of the vineyard, what will he do to the farmers those?

en.L: So when the master of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those farmers?"
en.B: Now when the owner of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those tenants?"
en.R: So what will the owner of the vineyard do to those farmers when he comes back?"

es.L: Entonces, cuando llegue el amo de la viña, ¿qué les hará a esos agricultores?».
es.B: Ahora bien, cuando venga el dueño de la viña, ¿qué hará con esos arrendatarios?».
es.R: Entonces, ¿qué hará el dueño de la viña con esos agricultores cuando regrese?».

fr.L: Quand donc viendra le maître de la vigne, que fera-t-il à ces vignerons-là ? »
fr.B: Quand le propriétaire de la vigne viendra, que fera-t-il donc à ces vignerons ? »
fr.R: Alors, que va faire le propriétaire de la vigne à ces cultivateurs quand il reviendra ? »

sw.L: Basi bwana wa shamba la mizabibu akija, atawafanyia nini wakulima hao?"
sw.B: Sasa, mwenye shamba la mizabibu atakapokuja, atawafanya nini wakulima hao?"
sw.R: Basi, mwenye shamba atakaporudi, atawafanya nini wakulima hao?"

decisions.choice: master: the owner of the vineyard
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the Lord, but in the story it means the owner. It hints at who the owner stands for.

decisions.choice: what will he do: Jesus lets the hearers pass judgment
decisions.reason: As in 21:28-31, the hearers give the verdict. They answer in 21:41.

source.text: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Κακοὺς κακῶς ἀπολέσει αὐτούς, καὶ τὸν ἀμπελῶνα ἐκδώσεται ἄλλοις γεωργοῖς, οἵτινες ἀποδώσουσιν αὐτῷ τοὺς καρποὺς ἐν τοῖς καιροῖς αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: They say to him, Bad men badly he will destroy them, and the vineyard he will rent out to other farmers, who will give to him the fruits in the seasons of them.

en.L: They say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "[Those] wretches he will destroy wretchedly, and he will lease the vineyard to other farmers, who will give him the fruits in their seasons."
en.B: They answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "He will put those evil men to a miserable death, and he will lease the vineyard to other tenants, who will hand over the fruit to him at each harvest."
en.R: They answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "He will kill those evil men in a terrible way. Then he will rent the vineyard to other farmers. They will give him his share of the grapes at harvest time."

es.L: Le dicen: «A [esos] malvados los destruirá malamente, y arrendará la viña a otros agricultores, que le entregarán los frutos en sus tiempos».
es.B: Ellos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} respondieron: «Hará morir de mala manera a esos malvados, y dará la viña en arriendo a otros que le entreguen el fruto en cada cosecha».
es.R: Ellos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} respondieron: «Matará a esos malvados de una manera terrible. Luego alquilará la viña a otros agricultores. Ellos le darán su parte de las uvas en el tiempo de la cosecha».

fr.L: Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} disent : « Ces misérables, il les fera périr misérablement, et il louera la vigne à d’autres vignerons, qui lui remettront les fruits en leur temps. »
fr.B: Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} répondirent : « Ces méchants, il les fera mourir d’une mort misérable, et il louera la vigne à d’autres vignerons, qui lui remettront le produit à chaque récolte. »
fr.R: Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont répondu : « Il fera mourir ces hommes mauvais d’une manière terrible. Puis il louera la vigne à d’autres cultivateurs. Ils lui donneront sa part du raisin au moment de la récolte. »

sw.L: Wanamwambia, "Wale wabaya atawaangamiza vibaya, na shamba la mizabibu atawapa wakulima wengine kwa kukodi, ambao watampa matunda katika majira yake."
sw.B: Wakamjibu, "Atawaua watu hao waovu kwa kifo kibaya, na shamba la mizabibu atawakodishia wakulima wengine, watakaompa mavuno kila msimu wa mavuno."
sw.R: Wakamjibu, "Atawaua watu hao waovu kwa njia ya kutisha. Kisha atawakodishia wakulima wengine shamba hilo. Wao watampa sehemu yake ya zabibu wakati wa mavuno."

decisions.choice: bad men badly: a play on words, the evil end of evil men
decisions.reason: The adjective and the adverb come from the same word. The punishment matches the crime.

decisions.choice: the hearers pronounce their own sentence
decisions.reason: The chief priests and elders (21:23) give the verdict on the tenants before they see that the story is about them (21:45), as David did before Nathan (2 Samuel 12:5-7).

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: put those evil men to a miserable death (B); kill those evil men in a terrible way (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the link between the men and their end without the repeated word.

decisions.choice: malvados ... malamente (L); de mala manera a esos malvados (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek plays on "bad" and "badly" (meaning decision m1). "Malvados" and "malamente" or "de mala manera" keep the echo in Spanish. The "le" at the start of the Literal sentence is written plain; it is Jesus.

decisions.choice: Ces misérables, il les fera périr misérablement (L)
alternatives: Ces méchants, il les fera périr méchamment
decisions.reason: French can keep the play on words (m1) with "misérables ... misérablement", which says both their wickedness and their wretched end; "méchamment" would mean that the owner acts with malice.

decisions.choice: wabaya ... vibaya (bad ones ... badly)
decisions.reason: The Greek plays on "bad" and "badly" (meaning decision m1). Swahili "wabaya" and "vibaya" share a stem, so Literal keeps the echo; Balanced and Readable say the sense plainly, as the English does.

source.text: Λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Οὐδέποτε ἀνέγνωτε ἐν ταῖς γραφαῖς· Λίθον ὃν ἀπεδοκίμασαν οἱ οἰκοδομοῦντες οὗτος ἐγενήθη εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας· παρὰ κυρίου ἐγένετο αὕτη, καὶ ἔστιν θαυμαστὴ ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς ἡμῶν;

records.literal_gloss: Says to them the Jesus, Never did you read in the Scriptures, A stone which rejected the building ones, this became into head of corner; from Lord came this, and it is marvelous in eyes of us?

en.L: Jesus says to them, "Have you never read in the Scriptures, '[The] stone that the builders rejected, this has become [the] head of [the] corner; from [the] Lord this came about, and it is marvelous in our eyes'?
en.B: Jesus said to them, "Did you never read this in the Scriptures: 'The very stone the builders turned down has become the cornerstone. The Lord has brought this about, and we look on it with wonder'?
en.R: Jesus said to them, "Surely you have read this in the Scriptures: 'The stone that the builders did not want has become the most important stone in the building. The Lord did this, and it is wonderful to us.'

es.L: Jesús les dice: «¿Nunca {{plural_you:leyeron|leísteis}} en las Escrituras: “La piedra que rechazaron los constructores, esta ha llegado a ser cabeza de [la] esquina; de parte del Señor sucedió esto, y es admirable a nuestros ojos”?
es.B: Jesús les dijo: «¿Nunca {{plural_you:leyeron|leísteis}} esto en las Escrituras: “La misma piedra que los constructores descartaron ha llegado a ser la piedra angular. Esto lo ha hecho el Señor, y lo miramos con asombro”?
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «Seguro que {{plural_you:han leído|habéis leído}} esto en las Escrituras: “La piedra que los constructores no quisieron ha llegado a ser la piedra más importante del edificio. El Señor hizo esto, y para nosotros es algo maravilloso”.

fr.L: Jésus leur dit : « N’avez-vous jamais lu dans les Écritures : “La pierre que ceux qui bâtissaient ont rejetée, celle-ci est devenue la tête de l’angle ; cela est venu du Seigneur, et c’est merveilleux à nos yeux” ?
fr.B: Jésus leur dit : « N’avez-vous jamais lu ce passage des Écritures : “La pierre même que les bâtisseurs ont écartée est devenue la pierre maîtresse de l’angle. C’est l’œuvre du Seigneur, et nous la regardons avec émerveillement” ?
fr.R: Jésus leur a dit : « Vous avez sûrement lu ce que disent les Écritures : “Les bâtisseurs n’ont pas voulu d’une certaine pierre. Mais elle est devenue la pierre la plus importante de la construction. C’est le Seigneur qui a fait cela, et nous en sommes émerveillés.”

sw.L: Yesu anawaambia, "Je, hamjawahi kusoma katika Maandiko, 'Jiwe ambalo wajenzi walilikataa, hilo limefanyika kichwa cha pembe; jambo hili limefanyika na Bwana, nalo ni la kustaajabisha mbele ya macho yetu'?
sw.B: Yesu akawaambia, "Je, hamjawahi kusoma maneno haya katika Maandiko: 'Lile jiwe ambalo wajenzi walilikataa limekuwa jiwe la msingi la pembeni. Bwana ndiye aliyefanya jambo hili, nasi tunalitazama kwa mshangao'?
sw.R: Yesu akawaambia, "Hakika mmesoma maneno haya katika Maandiko: 'Jiwe ambalo wajenzi hawakulitaka limekuwa jiwe muhimu kuliko yote katika jengo. Bwana amefanya jambo hili, nalo ni la ajabu kwetu.'

decisions.reason: The words come from the same psalm the crowds sang in 21:9. Where Matthew has "Lord", the Hebrew has God's name, the LORD.

decisions.choice: the rejected stone: Jesus, rejected by the leaders and made chief by God
decisions.reason: The builders are the leaders who reject the son, as in the parable. Peter applies the verse to Jesus' death and resurrection (Acts 4:11; 1 Peter 2:7).

decisions.choice: head of the corner: the main stone that holds the corner
alternatives: the top stone over an arch
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean a cornerstone at the base or a capstone at the top. Either way it is the stone the whole building depends on.

decisions.choice: this came from the Lord: God has done it
alternatives: the stone came from the Lord
decisions.reason: "This" refers to the whole turn of events, the rejected stone becoming the chief one.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
decisions.reason: The question expects yes; Readable states it, as in 21:16.

source.text: διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἀρθήσεται ἀφ’ ὑμῶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ δοθήσεται ἔθνει ποιοῦντι τοὺς καρποὺς αὐτῆς.

records.literal_gloss: Because of this I say to you that will be taken away from you the kingdom of the God and it will be given to a people producing the fruits of it.

en.L: Because of this I tell you that the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and will be given to a people producing its fruits.
en.B: This is why I tell you: you will lose the kingdom of God. It will be taken from you and given to a people that bears the fruit it calls for.
en.R: So I tell you this: God's kingdom will be taken away from you. It will be given to people who produce the fruit it should have.

es.L: Por eso {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que será quitado de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} el reino de Dios y será dado a un pueblo que produzca sus frutos.
es.B: Por eso {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: {{plural_you:ustedes van|vosotros vais}} a perder el reino de Dios. Se {{plural_you:les|os}} quitará y se le dará a un pueblo que dé el fruto que el reino pide.
es.R: Así que {{plural_you:les|os}} digo esto: el reino de Dios se {{plural_you:les|os}} va a quitar. Se le dará a gente que produzca el fruto que debe dar.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi je vous dis que le royaume de Dieu vous sera enlevé et sera donné à un peuple qui en produit les fruits.
fr.B: Voilà pourquoi je vous le dis : vous perdrez le royaume de Dieu. Il vous sera enlevé et sera donné à un peuple qui en portera les fruits.
fr.R: Alors je vous dis ceci : le royaume de Dieu vous sera enlevé. Il sera donné à un peuple qui produira les fruits que Dieu attend.

sw.L: Kwa sababu hiyo nawaambia kwamba utachukuliwa kutoka kwenu ufalme wa Mungu, na kupewa watu wanaozaa matunda yake.
sw.B: Ndiyo maana nawaambia: mtaupoteza ufalme wa Mungu. Utachukuliwa kutoka kwenu na kupewa watu wanaozaa matunda unayodai.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo nawaambia hivi: ufalme wa Mungu utachukuliwa kutoka kwenu. Utapewa watu watakaozaa matunda yanayofaa ufalme huo.

decisions.choice: a people: a new community that does God's will
alternatives: the Gentiles in place of Israel
decisions.reason: The word is often used of nations. Here it is the people, of any background, who bear the kingdom's fruit, like the tax collectors who believed (21:31-32).

decisions.choice: its fruits: the deeds the kingdom calls for
decisions.reason: Fruit is a picture of a life that matches repentance (3:8; 7:16-20), the fruit the owner came to collect (21:34).

decisions.choice: will be taken away from you: from the leaders who are listening
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the chief priests and elders (21:23), and they know he means them (21:45).

decisions.choice: God's kingdom
decisions.reason: Readable uses the shorter form.

decisions.choice: un pueblo
decisions.reason: The word can mean a nation, but here it is a people that does God's will (meaning decision m1), not another country. "Pueblo" says that; "nación" would suggest a state.

decisions.choice: un peuple at every level
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the nations, but here it names a new people that does God's will (m1); French "une nation" would suggest a country, so every level says "un peuple", as the English does.

decisions.choice: watu (a people)
decisions.reason: The word can mean a nation, but here it is a people that does God's will (meaning decision m1), not another country. "Taifa" would suggest a state; "watu" says a people.

source.text: Καὶ ὁ πεσὼν ἐπὶ τὸν λίθον τοῦτον συνθλασθήσεται· ἐφ’ ὃν δ’ ἂν πέσῃ λικμήσει αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And the having fallen on the stone this will be broken to pieces; on whomever but it may fall, it will crush him.

en.L: And the one who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces; and on whomever it falls, it will crush {{gender:them|him}}."
en.B: Whoever falls on this stone will be dashed to pieces, and if it falls on anyone, it will crush {{gender:them|him}} to dust."
en.R: Anyone who falls on this stone will be broken into pieces. And if the stone falls on someone, it will crush that person."

es.L: Y el que caiga sobre esta piedra será hecho pedazos; y sobre quien ella caiga, lo triturará».
es.B: Quien caiga sobre esta piedra quedará hecho pedazos, y si ella cae sobre alguien, lo reducirá a polvo».
es.R: Cualquiera que caiga sobre esta piedra se hará pedazos. Y si la piedra cae sobre alguien, lo aplastará».

fr.L: Et celui qui tombe sur cette pierre sera brisé ; et celui sur qui elle tombera, elle l’écrasera. »
fr.B: Celui qui tombera sur cette pierre sera mis en pièces, et celui sur qui elle tombera, elle le réduira en poussière. »
fr.R: Quiconque tombera sur cette pierre sera brisé en morceaux. Et si la pierre tombe sur quelqu’un, elle l’écrasera. »

sw.L: Na mtu atakayeanguka juu ya jiwe hili atavunjika vipande vipande; na yeyote ambaye jiwe hilo litamwangukia, litamponda kuwa unga."
sw.B: Mtu yeyote atakayeanguka juu ya jiwe hili atavunjika vipande vipande, na likimwangukia mtu yeyote, litamponda kuwa vumbi."
sw.R: Mtu yeyote atakayeanguka juu ya jiwe hili atavunjika vipande. Na jiwe hilo likimwangukia mtu, litamponda kabisa."

decisions.choice: the verse is included, as in the SBLGNT
alternatives: the verse is left out, as in some manuscripts
decisions.reason: A few early witnesses lack this verse, and some think it was added from Luke 20:18, which is very similar. Most manuscripts, including important early ones, have it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the stone that breaks and crushes: Isaiah 8:14-15 and Daniel 2:34-35, 44-45
decisions.reason: In Isaiah the LORD is a stone over which many stumble and are broken. In Daniel a stone not cut by human hands crushes the kingdoms of the world.

decisions.choice: crush: grind to powder, scatter like chaff
decisions.reason: The verb was used of winnowing grain. The Greek Old Testament uses it in Daniel 2:44 of God's kingdom crushing all others.

decisions.choice: no gender setting on "lo"
decisions.reason: The English offers "him" as the traditional alternative to "them". Spanish "lo" after "quien" and "alguien" is already the general form, so the setting has nothing to change.

decisions.choice: "celui sur qui elle tombera, elle l’écrasera" with no gender span
decisions.reason: As the style guide says, "celui qui" already means anyone in French, and the "le" that refers back to it is ordinary generic French, so French needs no setting where English chooses between "them" and "him".

source.text: Καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι τὰς παραβολὰς αὐτοῦ ἔγνωσαν ὅτι περὶ αὐτῶν λέγει·

records.literal_gloss: And having heard the chief priests and the Pharisees the parables of him they knew that about them he speaks;

en.L: And when the chief priests and the Pharisees heard {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} parables, they knew that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was speaking about them.
en.B: The chief priests and the Pharisees heard {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} parables and realized that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} meant them.
en.R: The leading priests and the Pharisees heard the stories Jesus told. They knew {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was talking about them.

es.L: Y al oír los jefes de los sacerdotes y los fariseos {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} parábolas, entendieron que hablaba de ellos.
es.B: Los jefes de los sacerdotes y los fariseos oyeron {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} parábolas y se dieron cuenta de que se refería a ellos.
es.R: Los jefes de los sacerdotes y los fariseos oyeron las historias que Jesús contó. Sabían que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} estaba hablando de ellos.

fr.L: Et les chefs des prêtres et les Pharisiens, ayant entendu {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} paraboles, comprirent qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} parlait d’eux.
fr.B: Les chefs des prêtres et les Pharisiens, en entendant {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} paraboles, comprirent que c’était d’eux qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} parlait.
fr.R: Les chefs des prêtres et les Pharisiens ont entendu les histoires que Jésus racontait. Ils ont compris qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} parlait d’eux.

sw.L: Na baada ya kusikia mifano {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, wakuu wa makuhani na Mafarisayo walijua kwamba anazungumza kuwahusu wao.
sw.B: Wakuu wa makuhani na Mafarisayo walisikia mifano {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, wakaelewa kwamba alikuwa akiwalenga wao.
sw.R: Wakuu wa makuhani na Mafarisayo walisikia hadithi alizosimulia Yesu. Walijua kwamba alikuwa akisema habari zao.

decisions.choice: his parables: the two sons and the tenants, and perhaps the stone
decisions.reason: The plural takes in the stories just told in the temple.

decisions.choice: he was speaking: present in the Greek, as reported thought
decisions.reason: Greek keeps the tense of the original thought: "he is speaking about us".

decisions.choice: the stories Jesus told
decisions.reason: Readable uses "stories" for parables, as in 21:33, and names Jesus.

decisions.choice: los jefes de los sacerdotes; los fariseos
decisions.reason: The terms used for these groups throughout Matthew, recorded once in this passage.

decisions.choice: wakuu wa makuhani; Mafarisayo
decisions.reason: The terms used for these groups throughout Matthew, recorded once in this passage. Literal keeps the Greek present "anazungumza" (he is speaking) as reported thought (meaning decision m2).

source.text: καὶ ζητοῦντες αὐτὸν κρατῆσαι ἐφοβήθησαν τοὺς ὄχλους, ἐπεὶ εἰς προφήτην αὐτὸν εἶχον.

records.literal_gloss: And seeking him to seize they feared the crowds, since as a prophet him they were holding.

en.L: And seeking to seize {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they feared the crowds, because they held {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as a prophet.
en.B: They wanted to arrest {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but they were afraid of the crowds, who regarded {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as a prophet.
en.R: They wanted to arrest Jesus. But they were afraid of the crowds, because the people thought {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was a prophet.

es.L: Y aunque {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} buscaban apresar, temieron a las multitudes, porque {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} consideraban un profeta.
es.B: Ellos {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} querían arrestar, pero tenían miedo de la gente, que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} consideraba un profeta.
es.R: Querían arrestar a Jesús. Pero tenían miedo de la gente, porque la gente pensaba que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} era un profeta.

fr.L: Et cherchant à {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} saisir, ils craignirent les foules, parce qu’elles {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} tenaient pour un prophète.
fr.B: Ils voulaient {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}arrêter, mais ils avaient peur des foules, qui {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} considéraient comme un prophète.
fr.R: Ils voulaient arrêter Jésus. Mais ils avaient peur des foules, parce que les gens pensaient qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était un prophète.

sw.L: Na wakitaka kumkamata, waliuogopa umati wa watu, kwa kuwa walimhesabu kama nabii.
sw.B: Walitaka kumtia mbaroni, lakini waliogopa umati wa watu, kwa kuwa watu walimchukulia kuwa nabii.
sw.R: Walitaka kumkamata Yesu. Lakini waliogopa umati wa watu, kwa sababu watu waliamini kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni nabii.

decisions.choice: seeking to seize him: they wanted to arrest him but held back
decisions.reason: The participle gives their aim; their fear of the crowds kept them from acting then (see 26:4-5).

decisions.choice: held him as a prophet: the same regard the crowds had for John
alternatives: they thought he was the Messiah
decisions.reason: The leaders fear the crowds over Jesus just as they feared them over John (21:26). The crowds called him the prophet in 21:11.

decisions.choice: lo before the verb (lo buscaban, lo querían)
decisions.reason: Spanish may put "lo" before the verb or join it to the end ("arrestarlo"). The separate "lo" is chosen so that it can take the deity_pronoun setting the English has.
